question: In ΔABC, right-angled at B, if tan A = (1)/(2), then the value of frac{{sin A( {cos A {{ - }} {{cos C}}} )}}{{cos C( {sin C - sin A} )}} is:
solution:
**Given:**

tan A = (1)/(2)

**Concept used:**

tanθ = P/B

sinθ = P/H

cosθ = B/H

Pythagoras Theorem:

Hypotenuse(H)² = Perpendicular(P)² + Base(B)²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e8414cd63ece4c9012c3e2dac6c80030b5e9407b3277dafd7873462dab55c28d.png] 

tan A = (1)/(2)

⇒ (P)/(B) = (1)/(2)

With the help of Pythagoras theorem we get,

H² = 1² + 2²

⇒ H² = 1 + 4

⇒ H² = 5

⇒ H = √5

Now,

frac{{sin A( {cos A {{ - }} {{cos C}}} )}}{{cos C( {sin C - sin A} )}} = ({frac{1)/(sqrt5)( {(2)/(sqrt5) {{ - }} {{(1)/(sqrt5)}}} )}}{{(1)/(sqrt5)( {(2)/(sqrt5) - (1)/(sqrt5)} )}}

⇒ ({frac{1)/(sqrt5)( {{{(1)/(sqrt5)}}} )}}{{(1)/(sqrt5)( {(1)/(sqrt5)} )}}

⇒ 1

**∴ Required answer is 1.**
